key: It is the way of Heaven not to strive, and yet it skilfully overcomes; not to speak, and yet it is skilful in obtaining a reply; does not call, and yet men come to it of themselves.
s: Weighing daring against not daring, the chapter turns to Heaven’s way; Wang Bi, on chapter 73, reads it as uncontested because it does not contend, answering with fortune for compliance and misfortune for defiance, and dwelling low, so things return of themselves.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 73, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

evidence.words: 天唯不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。…順則吉，逆則凶，不言而善應也。…處下則物自歸。
evidence.gloss: (On not striving yet overcoming:) Heaven simply does not contend, and so nothing in the world can contend with it. … (On not speaking yet answering:) Go along with it and there is good fortune, go against it and there is misfortune: that is not speaking and yet answering well. … (On not calling yet men come:) It dwells below, and so things return to it of themselves.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 73, at [72]); it renders Wang Bi’s base lines 天之道，不爭而善勝，不言而善應，不召而自來, identical in his text. Read his comment on the whole chapter: his three comments on these three lines carry each part of the reading (Heaven does not contend so none contends with it; compliance brings fortune and defiance misfortune, which is its answering without speech; dwelling below, things return of themselves). Plain sense (daring and not daring, then Heaven’s way) matches day.js and repeats no four words of the key. Entry-check ok.
